newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat tradeless in firm mkt and new crop focus.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat tradeless in firm mkt and new crop focus.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures did not trade on Monday but near-term settlement prices edged up in line with higher Australian Wheat Board pool prices and on emerging concern about dry Australian conditions.
Near-term settlement prices advanced by A$1.00-A$1.50 while more distant contracts fell by A$1.00 a tonne.

Gary Booth, of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd, said that while Queensland and northern New South Wales (NSW) faced reasonable conditions for the winter crop, the moisture profile in NSW was patchy.
But conditions in southern NSW, Victoria and South Australia were remarkably dry, with some frosts already occurring.
"(There is some) quite substantial concern about upcoming dry conditions (with) some people concerned that in certain areas we are moving towards droughtish conditions," he said.

The new crop in its early phase had a month to receive rain. A lack of rain in the next few weeks would raise real concern about the season's direction and lateness, he said. This could produce a tighter domestic market.
Rain in the next few weeks would leave forecasts optimistic for a crop of about 18.0 million tonnes, he said.
Rising prices would attract many growers into grain this season with other traditional markets of wool and meat still weak, he said.
World-wide demand for grain remained strong despite soybeans' slide in Chicago. Concerns in the grains market were on the supply side, he said.
